newsitem.title: BURMA: Burma government does not allow activists to meet.
newsitem.headline: Burma government does not allow activists to meet.

text.p: Burma's military government said it had prevented a top opposition politician from meeting supporters at the Shwedagon Pagoda, long a gathering point for democracy sympathisers.

The State Law and Order Restoration Council (SLORC) said in a statement received on Sunday that Tin Oo, deputy chairman of the National League for Democracy (NLD) party, was prevented from meeting supporters at the Buddhist shrine on Saturday afternoon.
Witnesses said several dozen NLD supporters had been waiting at the Shwedagon for him.
The shrine was the site of key pro-democracy speeches given by NLD leader Aung San Suu Kyi in 1988, the same year the military suppressed the democracy movement, killing and jailing thousands.
Nearly 100 police were deployed at the shrine, they said.
When Tin Oo arrived authorities refused his request to pay homage at the shrine, and forced him to leave without seeing the supporters, the statement said.
For the past four months, democracy supporters have gathered at street junctions near Suu Kyi's house on Saturdays and Sundays with the hope of hearing the Nobel Peace laureate speak.
The move to the street corners came after the SLORC blocked access to University Avenue, the street on which Suu Kyi's house is located, to prevent regular weekend speeches at her front gates.

The weekend speeches began in July 1995 after Suu Kyi was released from six years of house arrest. They grew in popularity, attracting up to about 10,000 people who came to hear Suu Kyi speak of democracy and efforts to achieve it in Burma.
Suu Kyi has been under virtual house arrest since December, when thousands of students took to the streets to demonstrate against the military government.
The government has accused Suu Kyi and the NLD of politicising the demonstrations for their own benefit. She has denied the accusations but said she supported the students' demand for justice.
Since the restrictions on her movements, Suu Kyi's has sent Tin Oo or other top NLD politicians to speak briefly to democracy supporters on the weekends.
Suu Kyi, placed under house arrest in 1989, led her NLD to victory in 1990 elections in a result never recognised by the military government.
